| `php:S4790` "weak hash" | `substr(md5($url), 0, N)` for cache keys / temp filenames | **Safe** — not crypto, just an identifier |

## Why this matters

Lifecycle scripts (`preinstall`, `install`, `postinstall`) are the #1 npm supply-chain attack vector. A compromised maintainer account or hijacked publish lets the attacker run arbitrary code on every developer machine and CI runner that installs the package — without any source change visible in the repo.

Defenses must be layered. No single control catches every attack class:
findings.message: Skill grants unrestricted tool access without appropriate constraints. An agent with unfettered tool access can perform arbitrary actions including file modification, network requests, and code execution.
findings.remediation: Restrict tool access to only the tools required for the skill's stated purpose. Use an explicit allowlist rather than granting blanket access.
